title: Jira vs Plane
comparison_markdown:
# Jira vs Plane (2026)

## Overview
Jira and Plane are two project management tools used by development teams to track and manage their work. This comparison is beneficial for teams currently using Jira who are looking for a more cost-effective or self-hosted solution, with the key reason to switch being the desire for greater control over their data and costs. The core use case for both tools is agile project planning and issue tracking.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Jira is a paid service with a per-user monthly fee, while Plane is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: With Plane, teams have full control over their data, whereas Jira stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Plane requires more technical expertise to set up and maintain, especially for self-hosting, whereas Jira offers a more straightforward cloud-based setup.
* Scalability: Jira is designed to scale with large teams and enterprises, while Plane's scalability depends on the team's self-hosting capabilities.
* Integration with Git: Jira has native integration with Git, while Plane relies on third-party integrations for Git support.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Jira | Plane |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $7.75-$14.50/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $387.50-$725/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,550-$2,900/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Jira:**
* Robust feature set for agile project planning
* Native integration with Git and other Atlassian tools
* Scalable and reliable cloud-based infrastructure
* User-friendly interface
* Extensive customer support
**Plane:**
* Free and self-hosted, reducing costs
* Full control over data and security
* Customizable and extensible through third-party integrations
* Open-source community support
* Limited native integrations and features compared to Jira

## When to Choose Each
Jira is the better choice for large teams or enterprises that require a robust, scalable, and reliable project management solution with native integrations and extensive customer support. Plane is suitable for smaller teams or organizations that value data control, customization, and cost-effectiveness, and are willing to invest time in setup and maintenance.

## Migration Path
1. Export Jira data in CSV or JSON format.
2. Use a third-party import tool or script to convert the data into Plane's compatible format.
3. Set up a Plane instance, either self-hosted or through a cloud provider.
4. Import the converted data into Plane using its API or import tool.
5. Configure Plane's settings and integrations to match the team's workflow.

## Our Take
Plane is not yet production-ready for most users due to its limited native features and integrations. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is Plane's reliance on third-party integrations for Git support, which may not be as seamless as Jira's native integration. However, for teams that value data control and cost-effectiveness, and are willing to invest time in setup and customization, Plane is a viable alternative to Jira.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) that do not need extensive native integrations
* Organizations with strict data control and security requirements
* Teams that prioritize cost-effectiveness and are willing to invest time in setup and maintenance
* Development teams that require customization and extensibility through third-party integrations
* Teams that do not need Jira's robust agile project planning features

## FAQ
### Is Plane free?
Yes, Plane is free and self-hosted, reducing costs for teams.
### Can I migrate my Jira data to Plane?
Yes, you can export Jira data in CSV or JSON format and import it into Plane using a third-party import tool or script.
### Does Plane have native integration with Git?
No, Plane relies on third-party integrations for Git support.
### Is Plane suitable for large teams?
Not yet, due to its limited native features and integrations, and scalability depending on self-hosting capabilities.
### Can I use Plane in the cloud?
Yes, you can set up a Plane instance through a cloud provider, but this may require additional setup and maintenance.

title: Trello vs WeKan
comparison_markdown:
# Trello vs WeKan (2026)

## Overview
Trello and WeKan are two popular project management tools used for organizing tasks and team collaboration. This comparison is beneficial for teams considering switching from Trello to WeKan, especially those valuing data ownership and self-hosting capabilities. The core use case for both tools is task management, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Trello offers a free plan with limited features, while WeKan is completely free as it is self-hosted.
* Data ownership: WeKan allows users to have full control over their data, whereas Trello stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: WeKan requires more technical expertise for setup, while Trello is user-friendly and easy to set up.
* Scalability: Trello is more scalable and can handle large teams, while WeKan's scalability depends on the server capabilities.
* Calendar integration: Trello has a built-in calendar view, while WeKan relies on third-party integrations for calendar functionality.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Trello | WeKan |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $5+/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $250/month (standard plan) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1000/month (standard plan) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Trello:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Scalable and suitable for large teams
* Built-in calendar view
* Integrates with many third-party apps
* Limited control over data ownership
**WeKan:**
* Completely free and self-hosted
* Full control over data ownership
* Customizable and flexible
* Open-source and community-driven
* Requires technical expertise for setup and maintenance

## When to Choose Each
Trello is suitable for teams that prioritize ease of use and scalability, and do not mind storing their data on Trello's servers. It is ideal for large teams with simple task management needs. WeKan, on the other hand, is perfect for teams that value data ownership and customization, and have the technical expertise to set up and maintain a self-hosted solution. It is ideal for small to medium-sized teams with complex task management needs.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Trello boards as JSON files using the Trello API or a third-party tool.
2. Set up a WeKan instance on your server and create a new board.
3. Use the WeKan import tool to import your Trello boards from the JSON files.
4. Configure your WeKan instance to match your Trello setup, including user permissions and board settings.
5. Test your WeKan instance to ensure that all features are working as expected.

## Our Take
WeKan is not yet production-ready for most users, as it requires technical expertise to set up and maintain. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that WeKan's scalability depends on the server capabilities, which can be a bottleneck for large teams. However, for teams that value data ownership and customization, WeKan is a great alternative to Trello, and we recommend switching to WeKan if you have the technical expertise and a small to medium-sized team.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) that value data ownership and customization
* Teams with simple task management needs that do not require scalability
* Teams with technical expertise that can set up and maintain a self-hosted solution
* Teams that do not need built-in calendar views or third-party integrations
* Teams that prioritize cost-effectiveness and do not mind self-hosting

## FAQ
### Is WeKan completely free?
Yes, WeKan is completely free and self-hosted, which means you can host it on your own server without paying any subscription fees.
### Can I migrate my Trello boards to WeKan?
Yes, you can migrate your Trello boards to WeKan using the Trello API or a third-party tool to export your boards as JSON files, and then importing them into WeKan.
### Is WeKan scalable?
WeKan's scalability depends on the server capabilities, which can be a bottleneck for large teams.
### Can I use WeKan for large teams?
While WeKan can be used for large teams, its scalability limitations may make it less suitable for very large teams.
### Is WeKan production-ready?
Not yet, as it requires technical expertise to set up and maintain, but it is a great alternative to Trello for teams that value data ownership and customization.

title: Dropbox vs Nextcloud
comparison_markdown:
# Dropbox vs Nextcloud (2026)

## Overview
Dropbox and Nextcloud are two popular cloud storage solutions that enable users to store, share, and collaborate on files. This comparison is beneficial for individuals and teams looking to switch from a proprietary cloud storage service to a self-hosted solution, with the core use case being secure and customizable file management. The key reason someone would switch is to gain control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Dropbox charges a monthly fee per user, while Nextcloud is free to use with self-hosting.
* Data ownership: Nextcloud allows users to retain full ownership and control over their data, whereas Dropbox's terms of service grant the company certain rights to user data.
* Setup complexity: Nextcloud requires more technical expertise to set up and configure, especially for self-hosting, compared to Dropbox's straightforward sign-up process.
* Scalability: Nextcloud is highly scalable, supporting large numbers of users and files, while Dropbox also supports large-scale deployments but with limitations on free accounts.
* Integration: Nextcloud has a built-in calendar and contact management feature, whereas Dropbox relies on third-party integrations for these functionalities.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Dropbox | Nextcloud |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $9.99-$16.58/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | Approximately $499.50-$829/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | Approximately $1999.60-$3316/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Dropbox:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Wide range of third-party integrations
* Robust security features
* Cross-platform compatibility
* Limited control over data and metadata
**Nextcloud:**
* Self-hosting option for full data control
* High scalability and customization
* Integrated calendar and contact management
* Free to use with self-hosting
* Requires technical expertise for setup and maintenance

## When to Choose Each
Dropbox is suitable for small to medium-sized teams that prioritize ease of use and don't require full control over their data. It's ideal for teams with simple file sharing and collaboration needs. On the other hand, Nextcloud is a better fit for larger teams or organizations that require high scalability, customization, and control over their data. It's also suitable for teams with advanced technical expertise and a need for self-hosting.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Dropbox data in a ZIP archive or using the Dropbox API.
2. Set up a Nextcloud instance on your own server or use a pre-configured appliance.
3. Use the Nextcloud WebDAV interface or the occ command-line tool to import your Dropbox data.
4. Configure any necessary integrations or plugins for calendar, contact, or other features.
5. Test your Nextcloud setup to ensure all data and features are working as expected.

## Our Take
Nextcloud is a production-ready solution for most users, offering a high degree of customization and control over data. However, it's essential to be aware of its technical limitations, such as the need for regular updates and maintenance to ensure security and stability. For teams that require a self-hosted solution with full control over their data, Nextcloud is an excellent choice, while Dropbox remains a better option for those prioritizing ease of use and simplicity.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) that don't require advanced features like calendar integration
* Medium-sized teams (10-50 users) with basic file sharing needs
* Large teams (over 50 users) with high scalability requirements
* Organizations with strict data control and compliance requirements
* Developers or power users who require advanced customization options

## FAQ
### Can I use Nextcloud with my existing Dropbox account?
No, you'll need to create a new account and migrate your data to Nextcloud. 
### Is Nextcloud compatible with all file types?
Yes, Nextcloud supports a wide range of file types, including documents, images, and videos. 
### Can I access my Nextcloud files offline?
Yes, Nextcloud offers desktop and mobile clients that allow offline access to your files. 
### Is Nextcloud secure?
Yes, Nextcloud has robust security features, including encryption, two-factor authentication, and access controls. 
### Can I integrate Nextcloud with other tools and services?
Yes, Nextcloud has a wide range of integrations with third-party tools and services, including calendar, contact, and task management apps.
meta_description: Nextcloud, a free self-hosted cloud storage solution, offers full data control and customization. See full comparison or Free migration guide.

title: Zoom vs Jitsi Meet
comparison_markdown:
# Zoom vs Jitsi Meet

## Overview

Zoom is the most widely used video conferencing platform. Jitsi Meet is a fully open-source alternative that runs in the browser with no account required and can be self-hosted for complete privacy.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Zoom free tier limits meetings to 40 minutes; Jitsi Meet is completely free
- **Account**: Jitsi Meet requires no account for participants; Zoom requires account or app
- **Privacy**: Self-hosted Jitsi is fully private; Zoom has had multiple privacy controversies
- **Features**: Zoom has more enterprise features like webinars and AI tools; Jitsi covers core needs
- **Self-hosting**: Jitsi deploys on a small VPS in minutes; Zoom cannot be self-hosted

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Zoom | Jitsi Meet |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | Free / $13.33+/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | See pricing page | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Zoom

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Jitsi Meet

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [jitsi/jitsi-meet](https://github.com/jitsi/jitsi-meet) * ~23k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Zoom if:** Zoom suits large organizations needing webinar features, enterprise phone systems, and HIPAA compliance.

**Choose Jitsi Meet if:** Jitsi is ideal for small teams, privacy-conscious users, or anyone wanting quick meetings without requiring participants to install software.

## Migration Path

No migration needed. Share a Jitsi meeting link instead of a Zoom link. Replace Zoom calendar links with Jitsi room URLs.

## Our Take

Jitsi Meet is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Zoom tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Jitsi Meet instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Zoom, switching to self-hosted Jitsi Meet will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Zoom until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Zoom paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Jitsi Meet free to use?
Yes. Jitsi Meet is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Zoom to Jitsi Meet?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Zoom data, follow the Jitsi Meet import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Jitsi Meet get regular updates?
Yes. Jitsi Meet has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Jitsi Meet without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Jitsi Meet development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced May 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Zoom](https://zoom.us) and [Jitsi Meet](https://jitsi.org) before making decisions.*
meta_description: Jitsi Meet is a free, self-hosted alternative to Zoom. Compare pricing, features, and migration steps. See full comparison.
